solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Native American private eye tailing city guide

indicators.note: tailing means following behind, so the detective comes after the street map

parts.note: an A-Z is a London street atlas, a city guide
TEC is short for detective, a private eye

explanation.surface: A detective shadowing a tour guide around a city, turning out to be Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the standard British street atlas of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were the people who ruled central Mexico before the Spanish conquest, an indigenous American nation.

clue.text: Sounds like former vithe-prethident'th ideology provides a means to solve problems

indicators.note: the clue tells us outright that what follows is an utterance heard, lisp included

parts.note: a lisped 'former vice-president's ideology': Al Gore was Bill Clinton's vice-president, and his -ism comes out as -ith

explanation.surface: Someone with a lisp describing a politician's creed as a problem-solving method.
explanation.walkthrough: The lisp is written into the clue itself, so 'Al Gore-ism' said that way becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A step-by-step procedure for computation or calculation is exactly a method of solving problems.

clue.text: Finish off mountain goat in between times in mountain region

indicators.note: the trimmed goat sits in between the two letters for times

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, here twice

indicators.note: finish off tells us to cut the end letter from the goat

parts.note: an ibex is a wild mountain goat

explanation.surface: Killing a mountain goat during a Himalayan trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' looks like 'kill', but it removes the last letter X from IBEX.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan plateau north of Nepal is the highest mountainous territory on Earth.

clue.text: One typically staying green provided note of hesitation in support of Conservative

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so the later pieces go below

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A hesitant voter staying loyal to the Green party, or perhaps backing the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Most cone-bearing trees such as pines and firs are evergreen, keeping their needles all year.

clue.text: Hopeful this composer performs after concert

indicators.note: after says the composer's piece follows the concert

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
the setter, who composed the clue, is I
to sing is to perform

explanation.surface: A composer optimistic after a concert performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This composer' is the crossword setter, who composed the puzzle, giving I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something showing signs of future success gives cause for hope, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Fan of loud music regularly skipped Bach

parts.note: punk is loud, aggressive rock music

indicators.note: every other letter of the name is skipped, keeping the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A punk rock fan who never listens to Bach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like an enthusiast; it is a swinging cloth fan of the Indian subcontinent.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cloth on a frame, swung by a servant to cool a room in colonial India.

clue.text: Something in the way former pupils win the ball, beginning to kick off

parts.note: OBs are old boys, former pupils of a school

indicators.note: off means taken away, so a letter leaves the word for winning the ball

parts.note: to tackle in football is to win the ball from an opponent

indicators.note: beginning to points at the first letter of kick

explanation.surface: Old boys playing a football match and winning the ball at kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to kick off' looks like the start of a match, but it says remove K from TACKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or barrier is a thing that stands in your path.

clue.text: Earnestly request playful fairy tales

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
lore is traditional stories and knowledge

explanation.surface: A child begging to hear playful fairy stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or beseech someone is to ask them urgently and with feeling.

clue.text: Being the one whose turn it is, I castle desperately, having limited freedom to move

parts.words: Being the one whose turn it is
parts.note: in cricket the batsman whose turn it is to bat is in

indicators.note: desperately suggests wild flailing, so the letters of 'I castle' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chess player whose move it is castling in desperation, hemmed in on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess misdirects: 'one whose turn it is' means batting in cricket, giving IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unable to stretch or yield is rigid and constrained in movement.

clue.text: Blow one's top with relish

parts.note: a gust is a blow of wind

indicators.note: top in a down entry is the first letter, the head of the word

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow one's top' is the idiom for losing your temper; split apart, it is GUST plus the top of 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty enjoyment or enthusiasm, as in eating with zest, is the meaning here.

clue.text: Try fruit flip

parts.note: to have a go is to try
bananas are fruit

explanation.surface: An invitation to try a fruit dessert, a banana flip.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is to lose one's temper or composure, the same as the slang phrase for going crazy.

clue.text: Crush journalists

definitions.meaning: to squeeze or squash something flat

explanation.surface: Suppressing the reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: One word both means to squeeze down hard and is the collective name for newspapers and their reporters.

clue.text: Head of Cosa Nostra supplanted by informer — it's essentially nuts

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of the crime syndicate as the part to go
supplanted by means replaced with, so the informer takes the letter's place

parts.note: the Cosa Nostra is the Sicilian Mafia
a rat is a grass or informer

explanation.surface: A mob boss ousted by a grass, which is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like 'crazy'; the definition means a thing made mainly of almonds.
explanation.definitionFit: This liqueur or biscuit is flavoured chiefly with almonds or kernels, so at heart it is nuts.

clue.text: May'em and trouble in fruit you slice open

parts.note: mayhem with its aitch dropped, as the clue's spelling shows, is havoc without its H
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A Cockney-style complaint about the chaos of cutting fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in May'em is the signal to drop the H from HAVOC too.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped green fruit is cut in half to remove its large stone before eating.

clue.text: Cheers! Prohibitionist drinking whisky — it's just for show

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the toast and teetotaller swallow a letter

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a dry is someone opposed to alcohol
whisky is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A teetotaller hypocritically toasting with whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Whisky is the radio code word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy but cheap and of poor quality, gaudy rather than substantial.

clue.text: One with judgment getting no credit over time

indicators.note: the trimmed judgment goes over, enclosing, the letter for time
getting no means losing the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: criticism is judgment of merit

explanation.surface: A wise person losing their credit over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' is the definition, as in 'that's a good one'. 'getting no' removes CR from CRITICISM, leaving ITICISM, which is placed 'over' T, holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever remark or quip is what is meant by 'a good one' when someone tells a joke.

clue.text: Net fully loaded with ease

indicators.note: loaded suggests something packed in and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishing net filled to the brim with little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something smoothly and effortlessly, especially speaking, is doing it easily.

clue.text: In the past, second person once strayed badly

parts.note: ye is the old plural form of you, the second person

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of 'strayed' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somebody who once went astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The day before today, or more broadly time gone by, used as an adverb.

clue.text: Warning sign where booze is sold — beer contains about 14 per cent of alcohol

parts.note: a wet area or county is one where alcohol sales are allowed

indicators.note: contains means the beer holds the letter within

parts.note: a pint is a measure of beer

indicators.note: one letter of seven is roughly fourteen per cent, the first of alcohol

explanation.surface: A pub sign about the alcohol content of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about 14 per cent of' picks one letter of the seven in ALCOHOL, its first, A.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice put up beside freshly decorated surfaces cautioning passers-by not to touch.

clue.text: Perhaps pirate broadcast silenced when it comes to receiver

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the airwaves, so we want what is heard

parts.words: silenced when it comes to receiver
parts.note: mute in ear: silent as far as the receiving organ, the ear, is concerned

explanation.surface: A pirate radio station broadcast cut off at the listener's end.
explanation.walkthrough: Pirate radio misleads; 'receiver' is the ear, giving the phrase mute in ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates who rose against their captain, as in tales of the high seas, are rebels on a ship.

clue.text: Bliss of North American touring Ireland with camper?

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the abbreviation goes round the rest

parts.note: a camper is a camper van

explanation.surface: An American's joy at touring Ireland in a camper van.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the state of perfect peace and happiness, used loosely for ecstasy.

clue.text: Disturbance when father comes to conciliation service

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
ACAS is the UK Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service

explanation.surface: A priest turning to mediation after a row.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is the British body that mediates in workplace disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy quarrel or brawl is a commotion.

clue.text: Official note on payment Her Majesty's accepted

indicators.note: on in a down entry places the note on top of what follows

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the payment holds the royal letters

parts.note: a fee is a payment
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: An official note about a payment the Queen has received.
explanation.definitionFit: This sports official enforces the rules in football and other games.

clue.text: Style acquired by unsophisticated person getting a trim

parts.note: got means acquired

indicators.note: a trim cuts the end off, removing the final letter

parts.note: a hick is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin acquiring style at the barber's.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval architectural manner of pointed arches, or a dark fashion, is a design mode.

clue.text: Incite outside right to provide support on the flank

indicators.note: the verb for inciting stands outside the abbreviation for right

parts.note: to stir up is to incite

explanation.surface: A political agitator rousing the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flank' suggests a military wing; it is the horse's side, where the rider's foot hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: The loop hanging from a saddle holds the rider's foot at the horse's side.

clue.text: Quietly stroke plant

parts.note: sh is the sound asking for quiet
to rub is to stroke

explanation.surface: Gently caressing a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush, a woody plant smaller than a tree, is a botanical example.

clue.text: Crime relating to handler

parts.note: of means concerning, relating to
a fence is a handler of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A crime involving someone dealing in stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach of the law, an illegal act, is a criminal wrong.

clue.text: As, Bs, Cs, Ds, Fs or Gs?

definitions.text: As, Bs, Cs, Ds, Fs or Gs?

parts.words: As, Bs, Cs, Ds, Fs or Gs
parts.note: these letters name musical tones, but the list leaves out E, so split 3,2 the answer says what the list lacks

explanation.surface: A list of exam grades or musical pitches.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,2 the answer describes the list itself: every letter of the scale except E.
explanation.definitionFit: A to G are the names of the musical tones of the scale, the pitches of written music.

clue.text: Indian food author listened to by some

indicators.note: listened to by some means in certain accents, said aloud

parts.note: a writer is an author

explanation.surface: An Indian cookery writer with a select audience.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic accents the word for an author can come out close to this dish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This yoghurt side dish with cucumber is served with curries in South Asian cuisine.

clue.text: Like legacy I wasted in the red

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters of 'I' and 'in the red' are rearranged

explanation.surface: An heir who squandered their legacy and is now overdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something passed down by will, so it is received from a predecessor.

clue.text: A shortened cane attached to something blown up, full of hot air

indicators.note: attached to says the following pieces are joined after the explosive

parts.note: a bomb is blown up

indicators.note: shortened means cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a stick is a cane

explanation.surface: A cane strapped to an explosive, or a balloon inflated with hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompous, inflated language with little substance is windy rhetoric.

clue.text: Composition of Sturmabteilung as initially reported

indicators.note: the storm troopers' name is to be read out by its initials, spoken letter by letter

parts.note: the Nazi storm troopers, the Sturmabteilung, were known as the SA

explanation.surface: A history composition about the Nazi storm troopers.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud as letters, S A is ess-ay.
explanation.definitionFit: A short piece of prose writing, such as a school assignment, is a written work.
